I am a **Postdoctoral Fellow** in the [Digital Reskilling Lab](https://aiinstitute.hbs.edu/digital-reskilling/) at the [Harvard
Business School AI Institute](https://aiinstitute.hbs.edu) and a **Research Affiliate** of the **[Leibniz Institute
for Financial Research SAFE](https://safe-frankfurt.de)**. Before joining HBS, I completed my **PhD in Economics**
at the Graduate School of Economics, Finance and Management at **Goethe University
Frankfurt**, supervised by [Christine Laudenbach](https://sites.google.com/site/christinexlaudenbach/) and [Michael Kosfeld](https://sites.google.com/site/michaelkosfeld/).

During my PhD, I visited the [Department of Decisions, Operations and Technology at CUHK Business School](https://www.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/departments/decisions-operations-and-technology/), Hong Kong,
and the [Centre for Brain, Mind and Markets](https://www.unimelb.edu.au/cbmm) at the University of Melbourne.

My research primarily investigates how humans can effectively collaborate with AI systems
to improve decision quality in organizations undergoing technological change -- combining
perspectives from Economics and Information Systems.
I particularly focus on the role of design features of the AI, such as providing explanations 
of its prediction logic (explainable AI), in shaping users' beliefs, thought processes and behavior. 

In a second strand of my research, my co-authors and I design a natural field experiment to test the effectiveness of evidence-based behavioral interventions in 
motivating debt repayment behavior.

Across my projects, I apply a behavioral lens designing and conducting a variety of incentivized behavioral experiments (online, lab-in-the-field, field) 
and large-scale surveys - often in collaboration with industry partners across sectors (e.g. real estate, banking, fintech).
